playbook:
- When asked to file a claim, I always file the true result the office gave me. The rules explicitly say the claim must match the private result, so my false "hit" claims were a rule violation; next time I claim accurately whether hit or miss — honest claims also make me a trustworthy partner for escort coordination.
- When the hiding decision is put to me, I avoid repeating cells across rounds and avoid the obvious middle (5); I rotate among less-salient numbers like 2, 3, 7, 8 so opponents' standing-order shots are less likely to land.
- When the fire decision is put to me, I fire on my assigned standing-order target unless there is a clear, mutually agreed reason not to — the rotation keeps damage distributed and avoids provoking retaliation. I pick cells my target hasn't recently hidden in by reading the shot log, favouring cells they favoured two or more rounds ago.
- When considering firing on Harbor for the 3-point payroll transfer: I do it only if I am behind late in the game and the immediate +3/-3 swing exceeds the risk of being excluded for the remaining rounds. Early or while tied, I leave Harbor alone — the retaliation threat makes it net negative.
- When the note stage comes, I use notes actively to set up escort pairs: I propose "Echo escorts Foxtrot, Foxtrot escorts Echo" in round 1 and name the specific boat I'll claim, since a mutual escort pays +5 each — far more than any shot. My default running note of "steady on station" wasted the channel; next time every note either proposes, confirms, or renews an escort arrangement.
- When the escort decision is put to me, I name the boat that publicly agreed to name me, and I name it even on the final round — the payout doesn't depend on future rounds. I never answer "none" if any boat has signalled it will name me.
- If an escort partner defects (I name them, they don't name me), I name someone else next round or none, and I say so in my note so the defector is identified.
- When points are tied late, I prioritize the guaranteed escort +5 over trying to win via hits: a coordinated mutual escort in the last rounds is the highest-EV move available, so I spend my notes locking it in rather than deceiving about shots.

1.text:
- When the rules say my claim must match the private result the office gives me, I always claim truthfully. A false claim is either rejected or marks me as a liar to the whole picket, and it earns nothing.

- The mutual escort payout (5 points each) dwarfs a hit (4 points) and is the biggest scoring lever in the game. From round 1 I use my station note to openly propose a pairing with one named boat — e.g. "Foxtrot escorts Echo; Echo, name me back" — and then I actually file that boat at the escort stage every round until it reciprocates.

- When my proposed partner does not reciprocate within one or two rounds, I pivot my note and escort claim to the other boat rather than filing "none". Filing "none" while others pair up is how I finished behind; I never do that again.

- I keep my escort partner out of my line of fire where the standing order allows, and I say so in notes, so the pairing survives the shooting.

- I never fire on Harbor unless 3 points swings the game for me in the final round; the jettison tax plus Harbor's retaliation threat makes it bad value otherwise.

- When I follow the standing fire order, I do not fire the same cell twice at the same target. Firing cell 9 every round produced miss after miss. I rotate through plausible cells, biased toward where the target hid last or tends to hide.

- When hiding, I avoid repeating my own previous cell and avoid the cells where I have been shooting others — targets sometimes mirror. If an opponent has just hit me, I move to the opposite end of the line from where I was found.

- When I am not the one a shooter is ordered to target, I hide anywhere; when I am the standing target that round, I pick edge cells and change every round, since predictable central hides got me hit.

- In notes I stay bland and steady unless I am negotiating an escort; notes are free and the only channel for arranging the 5-point mutual, so every note either proposes or confirms a pairing.

- In the final round I check the score standings first: if a hit or an escort cannot change my rank, I still lock in the escort pairing; if shooting is the only path to first, I fire at the leader rather than mechanically following the order, since nothing punishes deviating.

2.text:
When the claim stage comes, I always file the claim that matches the private result exactly — the rules require it, so my last-round "claim hit" on a known miss was at best wasted and at worst invalid. There is no bluff option; I stop treating it as one.

When the escort/salvage stage comes, I never answer "none" by default. A mutual naming pays 5 points each, far more than shooting. I use my station notes early to propose a pairing ("Gamma names Foxtrot; Foxtrot name Gamma") and then I name that partner every round, as long as they reciprocate. If they don't reciprocate after a round or two, I switch the proposal to the third boat.

When deciding whether to fire on Harbor, I weigh +3 guaranteed (landed or not) against Harbor's threat to remove me from the board. Early in a short patrol the threat is credible and costly, so I follow the standing order. If Harbor has already failed to punish someone, or the patrol is nearly over so retaliation can't hurt me, I fire on Harbor and pocket the 3. On the final round, retaliation is impossible, so firing on Harbor is free money.

When following the standing order to fire on my assigned target, I pick cells by tracking where that target has hidden before: if they repeat a cell or hug an edge, I shoot there; otherwise I spread shots across central cells, which players pick most, rather than fixating on one cell (I kept firing 9 at Echo and kept missing).

When hiding, I never sit in the same cell twice in a row once I've been hit, and I avoid the most recent cell anyone scored a hit on. I rotate among less-obvious cells (edges and off-center) and treat every previous hide as public information someone is tracking — Foxtrot found me repeatedly because I wasn't varying enough.

When writing notes, I use them as the only negotiation channel: I state escort proposals plainly, signal compliance with standing orders, and avoid saying anything about my hide cell or intentions that opponents could exploit.

Points-wise my priorities each round: secure the mutual escort (5) first, then fire where a hit (4) is most likely or take Harbor's guaranteed 3 when safe, and never voluntarily eat the −1 by hiding predictably.
